# sourdough-hydration

Hydration is the ratio of water weight to flour weight in a dough, expressed as a percentage. Higher
hydration doughs are slacker, harder to shape, and tend to produce a more open, irregular crumb when
the bake goes well — but they punish inexperience more too, since a slack dough is much less
forgiving of a shaping mistake than a stiffer one.

Once tried a 90%+ dough that behaved closer to a thick batter than anything shapeable by hand — see
the starter log's hydration section for how that one went.

See also [[sourdough-glossary]].
